question: What is the relationship between GIMUN and GMC?
answer: GIMUN (Model United Nations) and GMC (GIKI Moot Court) are two concurrent flagship academic symposiums organized by the student leadership at Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute (GIKI), Topi. They share event dates, campus facilities, evening socials, and opening/closing ceremonies, while maintaining separate, rigorous competitive frameworks and judicial/diplomatic evaluations.

question: Who is eligible to participate in the symposiums?
answer: GIMUN welcomes delegates from secondary schools (A-Levels/F.Sc) through university undergraduate and postgraduate programs across Pakistan and abroad. GMC is open to enrolled students from university law faculties, law colleges, and authorized moot court societies (teams of 2 to 4 students).

question: Will participants receive official certificates?
answer: Yes. Every participant who attends the required committee sessions or pleading rounds receives a Certificate of Participation with an online verification link. Award winners (Best Delegate, Outstanding Delegate and Best Delegation for GIMUN; Best Memorial, Best Oralist and Champions for GMC) also receive certificates of distinction.

question: Does submitting the registration form charge my card or bank account?
answer: No. Registration through this web platform is strictly non-payment. GIMUN & GMC does not collect credit cards or bank payments online. Once your application or delegation roster is approved, our Organizing Committee will issue a formal acceptance letter and invoice with official university bank transfer instructions.

question: Can I apply as an individual delegate or only as part of an institutional delegation?
answer: For GIMUN, applicants may register either as an independent Individual Delegate or as part of an Institutional Delegation (2 to 20 delegates managed by a Head Delegate or Faculty Advisor). For GMC, registrations must be submitted as teams of 2 to 4 advocates (strictly 2 oralists plus optional researchers).

question: What is included in the delegate and team registration fees?
answer: Registration covers all committee and courtroom sessions, background guides or the moot problem, a delegate kit, lunch and tea on conference days, and entry to the evening social events. On-campus accommodation is available on request and is confirmed, with any charge, when your application is accepted.

question: What are the registration deadlines?
answer: GIMUN registrations close on {{GIMUN_DEADLINE}}, and GMC registrations close on {{GMC_DEADLINE}}. Because committee capacities and courtroom chambers are strictly capped to ensure competitive quality, registrations may close early once allocations are exhausted.

question: When and how are country and committee allocations released?
answer: Allocations are evaluated on a rolling basis following submission. The Academic Secretariat evaluates candidate experience and preferences (1st, 2nd, and 3rd choices) to balance committee dynamics. Confirmed allocations are dispatched to delegate emails alongside background guides.

question: What Rules of Procedure (ROP) govern GIMUN committees?
answer: GIMUN committees operate under modern Harvard/THIMUN-adapted parliamentary procedure, emphasizing substantively moderated caucuses, unmoderated working paper formation, and structured draft resolution amendments. A comprehensive ROP handbook is downloadable from our Resource Hub.

question: Are Position Papers mandatory for award eligibility?
answer: Yes. To be eligible for Best Delegate or Outstanding Diplomat distinctions, delegates must submit a compliant Position Paper to their committee chair directorate at least 7 days before Day 1. Guidelines and submission portals are specified in each committee background guide.

question: What citation format is required for GMC written memorials?
answer: All written memorials must adhere strictly to the Oxford University Standard for the Citation of Legal Authorities (OSCOLA) 4th Edition. Memorials must include title pages, tables of authorities, statements of jurisdiction, and summary of pleadings. Strict word count limits and penal deductions are enforced per the GMC Rules.

question: What is the team composition and oralist speaking order?
answer: Each team has 2 to 4 members. Two are designated Lead Oralist and Second Oralist; any others serve as researchers. Each side has 30 minutes, normally 15 minutes per oralist (each must speak for 12 to 18 minutes), and may reserve up to 3 minutes for rebuttal or sur-rebuttal.

question: How does the Bench Clarification process operate?
answer: Registered teams may submit questions regarding factual ambiguity in the Compromis via the online Clarification Portal on this website. The Bench Drafting Committee reviews queries and publishes authoritative addenda publicly on the Clarifications board on equal footing for all teams.

question: Is on-campus accommodation provided for outstation participants?
answer: Yes, on request and subject to availability. GIKI can house outstation participants in on-campus hostels with separate wings for male and female participants. Request accommodation in your application; the organizing team confirms places and any charge when your application is accepted.

question: How do outstation delegations reach the GIKI campus in Topi?
answer: GIKI is in Topi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, about 90 minutes from Islamabad via the M-1 Motorway (Swabi interchange). Any group transport arranged by the organizers will be announced on the Announcements page and emailed to accepted participants.

question: What are the campus security and entry protocols?
answer: The campus has controlled entry. Bring a photo ID (CNIC, B-Form or student card) and your registration confirmation or QR ticket. Delegations arriving by institutional bus should send the vehicle number to the organizing team in advance.

question: Can I get a refund if I cannot attend?
answer: Tell the organizing team as soon as possible. Requests received before the registration deadline are reviewed case by case; after the deadline, fees are generally not refundable because places and catering are already committed.

question: Can someone else take my place?
answer: Yes, with notice. Email the organizing team with your reference number and the substitute's details before the registration deadline so the roster and certificates show the right name.

question: How soon will I hear back after applying?
answer: You receive an automatic receipt with your reference number straight away. We reply to messages within 3 working days, and application decisions follow the review timeline announced on the Announcements page.

question: What is the dress code?
answer: Business formal (Western or traditional) for all committee sessions, courtroom rounds and ceremonies. Smart casual is fine for evening socials unless an event says otherwise.

question: What should I bring?
answer: A photo ID, your QR ticket (on your phone or printed), a laptop or notebook, your position paper or memorial materials, formal clothing, and any medication you need.

question: Can you provide an invitation letter for visa or institutional leave?
answer: Yes. Accepted participants can request an official invitation letter from the organizing team; include your full name as on your passport or ID and your reference number.

question: Can dietary or accessibility needs be accommodated?
answer: Yes. Note them in the dietary and accessibility field of the registration form, or email the organizing team, and we will confirm the arrangements with you.

question: Is there a code of conduct?
answer: Yes. All participants are expected to act with respect and academic integrity, follow campus rules and the instructions of chairs, judges and organizers. Harassment, discrimination and plagiarism lead to disqualification and may lead to removal from the event.
